query: How do you find yourself again?
why_in_two_sentences: Both PositivePsychology results are well-built (myth/fact take-away boxes, signs of an identity shift, a causes taxonomy, scientific review) but stay at the level of advice categories like reconnect with your values. Ours supplies the missing mechanism: a preference signal that fell out of use, rebuilt on choices small enough that nobody is watching, with the guilt afterward named in advance.
what_we_do_that_they_dont: Names the mechanism (a preference signal trained out of use) instead of listing self-discovery activities
Explains why the journal and the solo trip did not work, and why the big questions produce the most convincing false answers
Gives a starting protocol: small unobserved choices, notice the pull before acting, expect guilt afterward
Explains why boredom is the condition the signal needs
34 verbatim FAQs including after-breakup, after-divorce, and after-children variants

above_the_fold.ours: H1 is the query, the short answer gives the preference-signal protocol in four sentences, then recognition sentences; concrete before any scrolling.
above_the_fold.theirs: PositivePsychology opens with a Take-Away Trio myth/fact box (feeling lost means something is changing, not that something is wrong) under a scientifically-reviewed byline; an instant reframe with visible authority.

questions_they_answer_that_we_dont: Why do I feel lost even when my life looks fine from the outside?
Is losing your sense of self normal?
trust_signals: PositivePsychology shows named authors, a PhD scientific reviewer, and inline citations (Erikson, 1968); ours has no bylines or citations.
one_change_with_most_traffic_impact: Add the two missing FAQ phrasings (life looks fine from the outside; is losing your sense of self normal); they are the only coverage gaps against two strong same-domain competitors.
